newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells three-year dollar-indexed notes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells three-year dollar-indexed notes.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, sold 263 million reais of three-year dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D) paying an annual yield of 11.46 percent, dealers said.
The three-year notes are the longest-dated dollar-indexed paper offered by the Treasury, which hopes to lengthen average maturities on its debt.
The market, however, also saw the decision to sell longer-dated paper as an attempt to signal that the government would not change the current exchange rate policy.

Over the past few weeks, the forex market has speculated about a speedier decline in the reais-dollar mini-band to reduce Brazil's trade deficit. Until today, the longest-dated dollar-indexed Treasury paper was 24 months.
Holders of dollar-indexed NTN-Ds are protected against a possible speedier depreciation of the local currency because the paper pays a fixed rate of return plus variation in the exchange rate.
The Central Bank also sold 365 million reais of two-year NTN-Ds with an annual yield of 11.39 percent.
A total of 2.532 billion reais of 181-day National Treasury Letters (LTN), due Aug 1, 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.477 percent a month.
Some 1.473 billion reais were sold in 365-day LTNs, due Feb 1, 1998, at an overnight call money rate of 2.416 percent a month.

The Central Bank also sold 755 million reais of National Treasury Notes (NTN-H) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR). The notes, due Aug 1, 1997, pay annual yields of 12.63 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
